intro.title: Authentication & authorisation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple login system that demonstrates the difference between authentication and authorization. You will learn how to verify a user's identity (authentication) and then control what they can access based on their role (authorization). The core programming concept involves using conditional logic and state management to handle user credentials and permissions. You'll work with basic security constructs like password verification and role-based access control. By the end, you'll understand how to implement these essential security layers in a web application.
intro.usecase: Authentication and authorization are fundamental security patterns in nearly every real-world application that manages user data. For example, a banking dashboard requires users to log in (authentication) and then restricts access to account details and transaction features based on their verified identity (authorization). As a developer, you'll implement this to protect user profiles in social media apps, secure admin panels in content management systems, and control access to sensitive forms in healthcare or e-commerce platforms.
